reasons: The cited clause caps the Deliverable conformity warranty at fifteen days and then extinguishes all correction/refund obligations, which fails the fallback floor (30 days services / 90 days software), so 'deviation' is the correct classification rather than an acceptable fallback.

The redline is targeted and directionally correct: it raises the period to ninety (90) days and replaces the blanket cut-off with an express preservation of the Section 19.4 repair/replace/refund remedy for nonconformities reported during the period, matching the rule's redline guidance and model language without disturbing the already-adequate 19.1/19.3/19.4/19.5 provisions.

The failed deterministic check ('warranty period ≥ 90 days') is a phrasing artifact — the new text reads 'For ninety (90) days after delivery' — and the 0.547 changed-character ratio is justified because the rule requires rewriting the duration and deleting the obligation cut-off in a one-sentence clause.
The comment is accurate, cites the playbook position (90 days with a real remedy), explains the acceptance-window overlap rationale, and follows tone and prefix conventions.
